note: Shipped ABI profiles, transcribed from docs/analysis.md §4.6. calibrate.mjs uses these
ONLY as a cross-check (assertion (d)). The calibrator under test must never be given
them: a driver that reports `usedProfile: true` fails the run outright, because the
whole point of §8.9 is evidence that the calibrator solves layouts it has never seen.
Provenance matters for reading a mismatch. The §4.6 numbers were recovered by
disassembling untapped-scry and then live-validated (30/30 in §12.3, 21/21 in §12.3b,
60/60 in §12.4c) against Slay the Spire 2 — which runs a MODIFIED 4.5.1 engine. A stock
4.5.1 export template is not the same binary. So a disagreement on the
4.5.1-release-single cell has two readings, and the harness prints both rather than
picking one: (a) the calibrator is wrong, or (b) the stock template's Control layout
differs from the StS2 fork's. Only (a) blocks publishing.

comment: control.anchor is not read by scry; it is included because §4.6's cross-check against
upstream scene/gui/control.h places Data.anchor[4] immediately after Data.offset[4],
and a calibrator that mistakes anchor for offset would otherwise look correct on the
nodes whose anchors are all zero. Main.tscn's AnchoredWide exists to break that tie.
